section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
excerpt: We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to meet or exceed the competitor's mitigation standard but will not necessarily delay development or deployment.

excerpt: Earlier editions of our RSP defined "AI Safety Levels" with specific lists of required controls.
paraphrase: Prior RSP editions defined AI Safety Levels via specific control lists.

excerpt: We still use this concept to refer to, and distinguish between, present levels of risk mitigations—those that we maintain for existing AI models. (For example, our initial Risk Report uses this distinction.)
paraphrase: The ASL concept is still used to describe present mitigation levels for existing models, as in the initial Risk Report.

excerpt: However, when defining the risk mitigations needed for future levels of AI capability, we have found that providing a specific list of controls is overly rigid, and we instead prefer to focus on what sort of argument an AI developer should make (and what sorts of actors it should address) regarding the risk level from its systems.
paraphrase: For future capability levels, Anthropic prefers argument-based framing over rigid control lists.

excerpt: This and other italicized instances of "highly capable" use the term as defined in Section 3.6.
paraphrase: Footnote clarifies that italicized "highly capable" refers to the Section 3.6 definition.

excerpt: September 19, 2023 (RSP v1.0) RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The changelog notes RSP v1.0 was the initial version, dated September 19, 2023.

excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The 2024 update adopts a more flexible risk approach while retaining the adequate-safeguards commitment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key 2024 improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes, and new governance/external-input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The changelog will describe the most notable 2024 changes below.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models).
paraphrase: ASL now refers only to safeguard groups, not models as before.

excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: New concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards allow targeted rather than broad-category safeguard application.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The ARA threshold was replaced with an autonomous-capability checkpoint.
